answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to lock a refundable stake bond before it can earn, with the bond slashed when peers attest fraud. A new identity starts at dawn with zero reputation and must slowly build trust through verified completed work, so spinning up thousands of fakes means locking real capital for each one. Agents who vouch for a fraudster lose part of their own bond, so trust spreads like a ripple only through parties with skin in the game. There is no oasis of free identities: each fake costs money, making large-scale fakery unprofitable.
